codes.label: Non-compete / non-solicitation exposure
codes.definition: Whether his employment agreement or local law restricts him from soliciting or serving his current employer's customers, creating legal liability and reputational risk.

codes.label: Reliability of customer commitments
codes.definition: Whether verbal promises from customers who say they would follow him are firm enough, and whether he can get written commitments, deposits or a realistic conversion estimate before resigning.

codes.label: Testing demand before quitting
codes.definition: Whether he can validate the business and keep the move reversible by taking side jobs on evenings and weekends, negotiating reduced hours, or starting part time while still employed.

codes.label: Replacing family health insurance
codes.definition: The cost and availability of individual or marketplace coverage for his whole household after losing employer-provided insurance, and how that cost affects his break-even point.

codes.label: Spouse's income and involvement
codes.definition: How his wife's part-time income, hours or access to other coverage stabilizes the household, and whether she shares the decision and the risk.

codes.label: Startup capital and financing
codes.definition: Whether the roughly $35,000 for van, tools and insurance comes from savings or debt, and whether funding it leaves emergency and college funds intact.

codes.label: Cash reserve for irregular early income
codes.definition: Whether the family holds several months of household expenses beyond startup costs to cover slow months, delayed payments and the gap between finishing jobs and being paid.

codes.label: Income gap versus current salary
codes.definition: Whether realistic first-year net revenue from a solo business, after expenses and unbilled time, can match his steady $78,000 salary.

codes.label: Self-employment taxes and lost retirement match
codes.definition: The additional self-employment tax, quarterly estimated payments and loss of employer retirement contributions that shrink effective take-home pay compared with a salary.

codes.label: Unpaid business overhead and skills
codes.definition: Whether he has the skills and willingness to handle bidding, invoicing, scheduling, marketing, bookkeeping and collections, which consume unbilled hours and lower his effective hourly earnings.

codes.label: Pricing, demand and competition
codes.definition: Whether local demand and competitor pricing support rates that sustain a profitable one-person electrical business after overhead.

codes.label: Licensing, bonding and permits
codes.definition: Whether his electrical license covers independent contracting in his jurisdiction and what business registration, bonding or permits are required and what they cost and how long they take.

codes.label: Liability and business insurance coverage
codes.definition: The need for general liability, workers' compensation and related coverage, and his personal exposure for workmanship and damage claims without an employer's umbrella.

codes.label: Disability and life insurance for the earner
codes.definition: Whether he would carry his own disability income and life insurance, since employer-provided policies may not carry over and an injury would stop income entirely.

codes.label: Physical sustainability of solo trade work
codes.definition: Whether he can keep up the physical demands of solo electrical work over the next 15 to 20 years, and what happens to income if he is injured or ill.

codes.label: Equipment depreciation and ongoing costs
codes.definition: The ongoing maintenance, repair and replacement costs of the van and tools, which are recurring expenses beyond the initial purchase.

codes.label: College timing and financial aid
codes.definition: How the oldest child's college start in two years collides with the business's ramp-up, including tuition cash flow and how self-employment income and business assets affect financial aid.

codes.label: Leaving on good terms with the employer
codes.definition: How he exits his current contractor affects future referrals, subcontracting work, a fallback job and his reputation in a small trade community.

codes.label: Business structure choice
codes.definition: Whether to operate as a sole proprietorship or an LLC, weighing personal liability protection against cost and paperwork.

codes.label: Retirement and long-term earning impact
codes.definition: How the move affects his retirement savings, vesting, contribution ability and long-term earning potential, given he has time to recover from a setback.

codes.label: Personal fit, risk tolerance and family impact
codes.definition: Whether he wants to run a business rather than do skilled work, can tolerate income uncertainty and the on-call lifestyle, and how the time demands and risk affect his family.

codes.label: Fallback plan and decision triggers
codes.definition: Defining in advance what outcome, such as a revenue milestone, savings threshold or months of losses, would make him continue or return to employment.

codes.label: Moonlighting rule conflict
codes.definition: Whether the agency's rule against same-industry freelance work applies to this client, and whether her existing or planned freelance work could breach it and risk termination.

codes.label: Consequences of breaching the agency policy
codes.definition: The risk that violating the moonlighting rule costs her the job, severance, bonus, unvested equity or a future reference, and the value of getting a written waiver or exception first.

codes.label: Negotiating a middle path with the agency
codes.definition: Whether she can ask for a leave of absence, part-time or contract arrangement, conflict waiver, raise or delayed start that captures the upside with less risk than resigning outright.

codes.label: Contract is time-limited and not equivalent to salary
codes.definition: That $60,000 over six months annualizes to a misleading figure because it ends, so she must compare it against her recurring $92,000 salary and plan for the period after it expires.

codes.label: Single-client concentration risk
codes.definition: The danger that one client supplying most of her income could delay payment, reduce scope, cancel early or change budgets, and the need to line up other prospects.

codes.label: Contract terms and client reliability
codes.definition: Whether the offer has written scope, payment schedule, kill fee, renewal option, cancellation rights and IP ownership, and whether the client is financially stable and pays reliably.

codes.label: Why the client is making the offer
codes.definition: Whether the client may want a dependent vendor and could later reduce rates or leverage her exclusivity, so she should consider what the client gains from her going independent.

codes.label: Existing freelance income as a demand signal
codes.definition: Whether her current side income shows genuine independent demand and whether that client base can grow into several clients to replace a salary, including how existing clients react to a full-time switch.

codes.label: Savings runway adequacy
codes.definition: Whether eight months of expenses is enough to cover gaps between contracts, slow client payments and business setup costs once taxes, insurance and benefits are included.

codes.label: True net value after benefits and costs
codes.definition: How losing employer-paid health insurance, retirement match and paid leave, and bearing self-employment tax and business setup costs, reduces the real value of the contract compared with her salary.

codes.label: Non-compete and non-solicitation in her agency agreement
codes.definition: Whether her agency contract restricts her from working with former colleagues or clients after leaving, and how that affects her plans.

codes.label: Career capital, network and mentorship
codes.definition: What she gives up by leaving a senior agency role, including advancement, mentorship, peer critique, collaboration, large-scale projects and professional network.

codes.label: Reputation and future referrals from the agency
codes.definition: How the manner of her exit affects her standing in a small industry and whether the agency could remain a referral source, client or future employer.

codes.label: Forfeited unvested benefits and timing
codes.definition: Whether upcoming bonuses, reviews, promotions or retirement-plan vesting would be lost by leaving or moonlighting before they land.

codes.label: Fit with independent work and her goals
codes.definition: Whether she wants the sales, administration, income volatility, isolation and self-direction of independent work, and how it fits her long-term career goals and temperament.

codes.label: Reversibility and ability to return to agency work
codes.definition: How easily she could re-enter salaried agency work if freelancing falters, including keeping her portfolio, network and freelance relationships active.

codes.label: Tax and business setup for self-employment
codes.definition: Her need to handle self-employment tax, quarterly estimates, entity choice, and setup costs like software, equipment, workspace and accounting help.

codes.label: Intellectual property ownership of work
codes.definition: Who owns the design work produced during employment or under the contract, and whether she can reuse portfolio pieces when pitching independent clients.

codes.label: Low downside from age and no dependents
codes.definition: That being 34 with no dependents gives her more capacity to absorb a failed attempt, shifting the question to whether the career-security trade-off is worth the upside.

codes.label: Signaling and positioning of the exit story
codes.definition: How leaving for a single high-profile client versus building a broad independent base shapes the reputation and future positioning she carries, which can open or limit later opportunities.

codes.label: Type of work and portfolio direction
codes.definition: Whether independent work tends to shift offers toward price-driven projects, and whether this contract builds the portfolio and positioning she wants over the next decade.

codes.label: Market timing and demand trends in the specialty
codes.definition: Whether shifts in the field, such as AI tooling, client budgets and industry consolidation, make now a better or worse moment to go independent than her own read suggests.

codes.label: Underlying motivation behind the move
codes.definition: Whether she is really seeking autonomy, income growth or a change in the work itself, and whether this offer addresses that root motivation or only its most visible symptom.

codes.label: Inventory of dormant projects and unused skills
codes.definition: Whether the most valuable thing the move could unlock is work she has been putting off, such as unused portfolio pieces, side ideas and stored skills, rather than the contract itself.

codes.label: Experience and credibility as an enabling asset
codes.definition: Whether his years of experience, reputation and licensing give him the credibility and skills to make self-employment realistic, provided he manages the business side well.

codes.label: Income ceiling and scaling by hiring
codes.definition: Whether his earnings are capped by the hours he can physically work as a one-person business, so that growth depends on hiring or subcontracting, which changes the risk profile entirely.

codes.label: Dependency mapping of critical relationships
codes.definition: Which anchor customers, key suppliers or local economic conditions would collapse his income if they disappeared, since a small business is an interdependent system where one failure can cascade.

codes.label: Value of his referral network over equipment
codes.definition: That the trust and referral network he already holds is the real source of leverage, with the van and tools merely the means of converting that network into paying work.

codes.label: Lost employer-provided trade infrastructure
codes.definition: What he gives up beyond salary, such as apprenticeship pipelines, bonding relationships, supplier discounts and mentors who steer large commercial jobs to him, none of which a solo shop automatically inherits.
